newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-ANWAR HITS DAZZLING CENTURY AGAINST NEW ZEALAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ANWAR HITS DAZZLING CENTURY AGAINST NEW ZEALAND.

text.p: Acting captain Saeed Anwar struck a scintillating century to put Pakistan on course for a big first innings lead over New Zealand in the second test on Friday.

Anwar, leading the side in the absence of the injured WasimAkram, hit an unbeaten 115 as the Pakistanis shrugged off an early setback and cruised to 219 for one at tea on the second day in reply to New Zealand's first innings of 249.
Anwar's century, his fourth in tests, contained 16 sizzling boundaries and came off 146 balls. His second-wicket partner Ejaz Ahmed was 91 not out at the interval, having struck 14 fours.
Chris Cairns struck an early blow, tempting Pakistani opener Zahoor Elahi into fencing at an outswinger and getting him caught at first slip by Stephen Fleming with the total six.
But Anwar and Ejaz, after a cautious start, went on to punish the New Zealand attack almost at will.
New Zealand won the first of the two tests by 44 runs.
